Subject: Deployment pathing: Hosted vs Reserved capacity for Acme Payments

Hi Lena / Acme team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great alignment on the core assistant use case. I want to capture the items we discussed and a few clarifying questions so we can put together an actionable proposal (Hosted vs Reserved/Dedicated + fallback plan).

Summary of current understanding:
- Primary feature: customer support assistant (text generation) delivering short to medium responses; embeddings used for search but not latency-sensitive.
- Steady-state traffic: ~80 requests/sec (avg).
- Expected burst profile: spikes to ~400 RPS for 2–3 minute windows (events, promotions).
- Typical payload sizes: ~75 input tokens, ~150 output tokens.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required, 30-day retention for logs; potential future need for VPC/private deployment.
- Target SLO: P95 latency goal ~120ms (we discussed this as a stretch target).

Clarifying questions (can you confirm?):
1) Are the 400 RPS bursts simultaneous low-latency requests (i.e., each request expects response within the 120ms P95), or can those bursts tolerate higher tails?
2) Any hard SLA on uptime/availability beyond SOC2 compliance (e.g., payment flows that require sub-second guarantees)?
3) Expected token distribution during burst vs steady-state (do outputs grow during peak?).
4) Any regulatory/regional restrictions (data residency) beyond US-only today?

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm the burst is latency-sensitive, we'll run two parallel proposals:
  a) Hosted plan: recommended autoscaling + prefix/KV caching config and a short hosted stress-test to validate P95 under your pattern.
  b) Reserved/Dedicated plan: sizing for a reserved pool that targets 120ms P95 at peak (includes buffer), plus estimated cost and lead time.
- We'll include fallback policies (Hosted fallback if Dedicated capacity is saturated) and a short mutual action plan (MAP) for exec review.

Can you confirm the clarifying items above and let us know if Thursday morning (10:00 AM PST) works for a 30-minute follow-up to decide on a PoC approach?

Attachments: acme_req_snapshot.pdf (high-level reqs) — I'll attach a cleaned-up MAP in the next message.

Thanks,

- SLA: we don't have a formal financial SLA for this product today, but operationally we need reliable performance during peaks (customer-experience critical).
- Token distribution: we see small variance in outputs during peaks; median output ~140–160 tokens, occasional longer replies.
- Data residency: US only for now; may expand to EU next year. SOC2 compliance is required.

Numbers / asks:
- Steady-state 80 RPS (confirmed).
- Burst up to 400 RPS for up to ~3 minutes (confirmed) and those requests should target the P95 objective if possible.
- Target P95 goal: 120ms — this is our executive preference; we understand there may be tradeoffs.

We are open to a Hosted-first path if you can show via a short hosted load test that P95 under our pattern is within acceptable range. If not, we'll consider Reserved/Dedicated. Please include estimated cost delta and lead time for Dedicated in your proposal.

Thursday 10:00 AM PST works for a follow-up. Please include your engineering lead if possible.

Thanks Rachel — quick guidance below. Ill attach two note files with backing assumptions.

Short answer: Hosted can often hit reasonable P50/P90 numbers thanks to our autoscaling and KV/prefix caching, but for a strict P95 target of 120ms across sustained 400 RPS bursts we'll likely see tail degradation on hosted-only because of autoscaler lag and multi-tenant noisy neighbors. For that reason I recommend proposing both and positioning Dedicated as the safe path for a firm P95 at peak.

Sketch-level recommendations:
- Hosted (conservative config): enable continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, warm instances, and a burst-cap policy that pre-warms based on predicted events. Expected P95: ~140–220ms during peak bursts (high variance depending on exact concurrency and token lengths).

- Dedicated / Reserved (targeted sizing): assume we serve a medium transformer optimized model with quantization-friendly build. To hit 120ms P95 at 400 RPS with token sizes ~225 total we should target a reserved pool equivalent to ~6 x A100-class GPUs (or 10 x smaller T4-style instances depending on model family). This includes a 20% buffer.
  - Lead time: 2–4 weeks to reserve/provision and run perf tuning + canary.
  - Cost delta: estimated 2.2x–3.0x vs Hosted (varies by exact instance types and discounting).

Fallbacks / hybrid: propose Dedicated as primary with Hosted fallback policy (route overflow to Hosted with degraded SLO and throttling). Also propose a short benchmark POC: 24–48hr stress test that runs synthetic and real traffic to validate queuing and p95.

I'll drop the dedicated-sizing-notes.txt in the folder; Marissa, can you paste a draft price range for the slide? Rachel, I can own the one-slide sketch and exec-facing bullet points.

Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi Lena / team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on numbers and for agreeing to the Thursday slot. Based on our internal sizing discussion, here's a concise options summary and proposed next steps so your execs have a clear decision path.

Option 1 — Hosted-first (fastest ramp, lower upfront cost)
- What: Use Redwood Hosted API with autoscaling + prefix/KV caching and pre-warm policy for predictable events.
- Expected performance: P95 typically ~100–150ms at steady-state; during a 400 RPS burst we expect P95 in the ~150–220ms range depending on burst behavior and caching effectiveness.
- Pros: no provisioning lead time, lower short-term cost, simple onboarding.
- Cons: tail variability during sustained high bursts; no isolation guarantees.

Option 2 — Reserved / Dedicated (stable P95, predictable economics)
- What: Reserved GPU pool sized for your peak (proposal: ~6 A100-equivalent GPUs as an initial sketch; final sizing will depend on chosen model and quantization).
- Expected performance: P95 target achievable in the ~90–120ms range at 400 RPS with our recommended tuning.
- Lead time & cost: ~2–4 weeks to provision + perf tuning; estimated monthly cost 2.2x–3.0x Hosted (range depends on instance mix and discounting).
- Pros: predictable latency and isolation; can meet strict P95 targets.
- Cons: higher committed cost and longer lead time.

Recommended plan (for Thursday exec decision):
1) Run a 24–48hr Hosted stress test (no-cost first trial) to validate baseline tail behavior and caching impact.
2) If Hosted stress test cannot show P95 near 120ms under your burst profile, proceed with a Dedicated reservation (we'll scope exact GPU mix and price).
3) In either case, we propose a hybrid fallback: Dedicated primary with Hosted overflow routing + throttling to preserve stability.

Next steps:
- Redwood: I'll schedule the Hosted stress test (engineers will need a sample traffic replay).
- Acme: Send a 24hr sample of production-ish traffic or agree to let us replay anonymized traffic during the trial.
- Proposed follow-up: Thu 10:00 AM PST — 30 minutes to review stress test sketch and agree on PoC direction.

Attachments: Redwood-hosted-latency-notes.pdf (quick theory of operation), Acme-MAP-v1.pdf (mutual action plan draft), Redwood-dedicated-sku-grid.xlsx (pricing sketch).
